title: Adaptive Output Fidelity Compass — product requirements and rollout
author: Elena Park
body:
Overview:

Purpose
This document defines the Adaptive Output Fidelity Compass (AOFC): a productized decision framework and implementation PRD that guides runtime routing, model variant selection, and pricing/consumption signals to trade output fidelity for latency and cost across Redwood deployments (hosted, dedicated, private). AOFC is intended to be an operational control plane component used by: Redwood runtime, Console, Optimize advisor, and billing/usage pipelines.

Why this matters
- Customers need predictable outcomes when we change model variants, quantization, or batching that affect result fidelity.
- Many production apps are willing to accept reduced fidelity in exchange for deterministic latency and lower unit cost; we need a clear, auditable way to encode those tradeoffs.

Scope
In scope:
- Decision framework to pick fidelity tiers per-request based on route-level policy, tenant preferences, SLOs, and economic signals.
- Runtime API and config schema for per-route fidelity budgets and fallbacks.
- Telemetry and observable signals (fidelity metrics, regression counters, switch events).
- Console UX wireframes and Optimize integration for recommending defaults.
- Billing signal mapping for fidelity-based metering.

Out of scope:
- New model training or model architecture changes.
- Low-level kernel optimizations (handled by runtime kernel selection docs).

Goals and success metrics
Primary goals (product + measurable targets):
1) Reduce per-token cost by enabling fidelity tiering for 40% of eligible host routes within 6 months.
2) Keep fidelity regressions (customer-facing quality alerts) under 0.2% of requests that changed fidelity tier during rollout.
3) Decrease 95th-percentile latency by 15% for routes with fidelity-selected fallbacks under targeted traffic mixes.

Success metrics (signals we will track):
- Adoption: % of active customers who configure route-level fidelity budgets.
- Economics: delta in active route per-token spend after AOFC applied.
- Quality: eval-set BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-sim decline and customer-reported regressions.
- Reliability: fallback frequency and correctness of automatic compatibility checks.

High-level design
1) Policy model (decision tree):
- Input signals: route_SLO (latency target), tenant_budget_override, current_runtime_capacity, feature_flags, call_type (sync/stream), observed_quality_score (from light-weight eval hooks).
- Decision nodes: capacity_check -> budget_check -> quality_prediction -> variant_selection -> rate-limit-adjusted-execution.

ASCII decision tree (simplified):

  [request] 
     |-- capacity_ok? -- yes --> budget_remaining? -- yes --> select_target_variant --> execute
     |                             
     |                             no  --> select_lower_fidelity_variant --> execute
     |-- capacity_ok? -- no  --> select_lower_fidelity_variant (or queued burst)

2) Fidelity tiers and variant catalogue
- Fidelity-1 (baseline): original model, full precision quantization, default prompt.
- Fidelity-2 (economy): quantized model (4-bit/8-bit depending on architecture), trimmed context/window, lightweight decoding params.
- Fidelity-3 (low-cost): distilled/smaller variant or cached-answer-first policy with best-effort semantic quality.
- Compatibility matrix: each tier mapped to supported models and required runtime capabilities (KV cache hotness, quant profile id).

Requirements (must-have)
Present as a plain-text table for easy copy into spreadsheets: 

| id | requirement | acceptance criteria | owner | priority |
| R1 | Per-route fidelity budget schema | Routes can declare min/max fidelity tiers and preferred tradeoff (latency/cost/quality) via YAML/JSON. Example config validated by Console and API. | Product | P0 |
| R2 | Runtime variant selector API | Runtime exposes /select-variant(request_id, route_id, signals) and returns selected_variant_id + rationale. Latency of selector < 5ms median. | Runtime | P0 |
| R3 | Telemetry events and metrics | Emit fidelity.change, fidelity.failover, fidelity.quality_delta events. Metrics must be consumable by Console and alerting. | Eng Platform | P0 |
| R4 | Console UI for route budgets | Route settings page shows current budget, historical switch rate, and cost impact estimate. | DX | P1 |
| R5 | Billing mapping | Each fidelity tier has a metering factor (e.g., 1.0, 0.65, 0.38) that maps to token billing. Round-trip applied on invoice preview. | Finance | P1 |
| R6 | Safety and audit trail | All automatic tier changes must be recorded with rationale and linked evaluation snapshot. 30-day retention for audit. | Security | P1 |

Non-functional requirements
- Selector must be highly available with 99.99% uptime.
- Selector decision latency P95 < 20ms (including nearby cache lookups).
- Telemetry event delivery latency < 10s to Console ingestion pipeline.

API / config examples
1) Route fidelity budget (JSON):

{
  "route_id": "route-prod-chat-1",
  "fidelity_budget": {
    "min_tier": "Fidelity-2",
    "max_tier": "Fidelity-1",
    "monthly_cost_target": 2500,
    "quality_guardrails": {
      "semantic-drop_threshold": 0.04,
      "allowed_eval_regressions": 0.002
    }
  },
  "fallback_policy": "prefer_lower_cost_then_quality",
  "owner": "payments-team"
}

2) Selector call (example HTTP):

POST /v1/runtime/select-variant
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "request_id": "r_ABC123",
  "route_id": "route-prod-chat-1",
  "signals": {"latency_ms": 40, "queue_depth": 3, "tenant_credit_state": "ok"}
}

Response:
{
  "selected_variant": "gptx-16k-quant-4-F2",
  "tier": "Fidelity-2",
  "rationale": "capacity-constrained + budget-bound; predicted semantic drop 0.023"
}

Compatibility and runtime capabilities table (text):
- Fidelity-1: supported on GPU-v100+, kv-hotness >= 0.6, requires full-precision kernel set.
- Fidelity-2: supported on GPU-v100/rtx-a6000, quant-profile q4f, KV optional.
- Fidelity-3: CPU fallback allowed if latency SLO > 800ms; requires cached-prefix support.

Telemetry and observability
Must emit the following events with structured payloads (examples):
- fidelity.change (request_id, old_tier, new_tier, driver, reason)
- fidelity.quality_delta (request_id, eval_metric, predicted_delta)
- fidelity.failover (request_id, attempted_variant, fallback_variant, error)

Console needs: per-route historical chart for tier distribution, cost delta, and a "safety leash" toggle that blocks automatic demographic switches.

Quality monitoring and guardrails
- Lightweight eval harness runs continuous micro-evals on a sampled 0.5% of traffic per-route and computes semantic-drop and prompt-sensitivity metrics.
- Alerting rules: trigger advisor when semantic-drop > route.quality_guardrails.semantic-drop_threshold OR when customer-reported regressions spike > 5x baseline in 1d.

Pricing and billing implications
- Metering factor per-tier applied to token counters (configurable per-tenant override): default mapping Fidelity-1=1.0, Fidelity-2=0.65, Fidelity-3=0.35.
- Console invoice preview shows hypothetical charges if AOFC were enabled.
- Product must provide migration guidance for customers on Dedicated (reserved capacity) where per-token economics are amortized differently: include recommended commit adjustment strategies.

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Alpha (internal teams only, 6 weeks)
- Implement selector API and config validation.
- Add telemetry hooks and Console debug panel.
- Run internal smoke routes for cost/quality measurement.

2) Private beta (select customers, 8–12 weeks)
- Invite 6–8 customers across verticals (SaaS search, conversational assistant, docs summarization).
- Provide hand-holding: SLO tuning, billing previews, rollback paths.
- Measure quality regressions on customer-specific eval sets.

3) Gradual public rollout (6 months)
- Default to opt-out for high-risk regulated customers.
- Offer Optimize advisor recommendations and one-click enable.

Operational runbook excerpts (numbered checklist)
1) If fidelity.change rate suddenly spikes > 3x:
   1.1) Check selector health and recent config pushes (eng-platform).
   1.2) Look for upstream capacity events (gpu-fleet).
   1.3) If caused by recent config change, rollback to previous route budget and notify owner.

2) If quality.alert fires for a route: 
   2.1) Pause automatic downgrades for that route (safety leash).
   2.2) Kick off fast-eval-run on last 500 sample requests.
   2.3) Engage product + research for triage; consider targeted A/B rollback.

Security and compliance
- All selector decisions and evaluation snapshots saved to audit log with TTL 90 days by default; restricted customers may request extended retention.
- For Private deployments, AOFC decision logic can run in customer VPC by deploying the "selector-agent" container; we provide a signed OCI bundle and local telemetry bridge instructions.

UX mockups and Console integration (summary)
- Route settings: fidelity budget card, projected monthly cost slider, safety leash toggle, and "preview changes" modal.
- Console Advisor: per-route recommendation with one-click apply and simulated impact.

Dependencies
- Eng-serving-runtime: variant catalog and runtime capability discovery APIs.
- Eng-infra/gpu-fleet: capacity signals and burst windows.
- Billing & Finance: metering factor formal approval and invoice preview API.
- Optimize: integration for recommending per-route defaults.

Open questions (decisions to make)
- Q1: What is the default semantic-drop threshold that should be enforced for platform-wide auto-downgrades? (proposal: 0.03)
- Q2: How granular should metering factors be (per-variant vs per-tier)? (proposal: per-tier default with opt-in per-variant overrides)

Next steps and action items (short list)
- Product: finalize acceptance criteria for R1-R3 and prioritize JIRA epics (due 2026-06-18).
- Runtime: implement /select-variant prototype with rationale payload (due 2026-07-01).
- DX/Console: build prototype fidelity budget card in staging (due 2026-07-08).

Owners
- Product owner: Elena Park
- Runtime lead: Jared Liu
- Observability lead: Maya Thompson

Appendix: example YAML route snippet

route_id: route-prod-summarize-2
fidelity_budget:
  min_tier: Fidelity-2
  max_tier: Fidelity-1
  monthly_cost_target: 1000
  quality_guardrails:
    semantic-drop-threshold: 0.025
fallback_policy: prefer_quality
operator_notes: "Target high-throughput summarization with constrained cost budget. Enable safety leash for first 30 days."
